beats: Hook: every step, gigabytes of fresh weights have to jump from the GPUs that learn to the GPUs that talk. [line_weights_zipline]

Weight sync: trainers split the model one way (expert / pipeline parallel), generators another (tensor / data parallel), so the pieces must be re-sorted on the move. [line_reshelve_two_cases, line_card_catalog, line_cabinet_tower]

Point to point: each trainer sends its pieces straight to the generators that need them, not through one doorway (LlamaRL; a published weight transfer in under 2 seconds, check). [line_one_door_queue, line_pairs_pass_boxes]
Sizes: 10 GB+ of weights per sync (much more for the largest models, check) vs 1-100 MB of rollouts, rewards and metadata per batch. [line_crate_vs_envelope, line_postal_scale]
Agents: asked to book a trip, the model plans, calls tools (flights, hotel), reads the results and reports back. [line_agent_trip_desk, line_tap_two_people]
Agentic RL: tools and verifiers run on CPUs; the GPUs can end up queueing for them. [line_tool_desk_queue, line_whisper_line]

The whole plant: LLM server, agent loop, async rollout manager, data store, training engine, checkpoints, online quantization on the weight path. [line_rl_post_room, line_slip_boxes, line_servers, line_d_servers, line_gpu]

Who runs it: a single controller calling every step in order vs asynchronous dataflow (stations with in- and out-queues, no boss); the trend is towards dataflow, most systems are a mix. [line_foreman_whistle, line_intray_stations, line_manager]
Takeaway: the open problems are plumbing: generation speed, weight transfer, data transfer, CPU latency, the programming model. [line_rl_post_room, line_weights_zipline]
